slo_title: State and prove Parseval's identity for Fourier transforms

mcq.q: \(\text{For the function } f(x) = \begin{cases} a^2-x^2, & |x| \leq a \\ 0, & |x| > a \end{cases} \text{ with Fourier transform } F(s) = \frac{4}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \left( \frac{\sin(as)-as\cos(as)}{s^3} \right), \text{ use Parseval's identity to find } \int_0^\infty \left( \frac{\sin t - t\cos t}{t^3} \right)^2 dt.\)

\(\text{Given the Fourier transform pair } f(x) = \begin{cases} 1-|x|, & |x| \leq 1 \\ 0, & |x| > 1 \end{cases}, F(s) = \frac{4}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \left( \frac{\sin(s/2)}{s} \right)^2, \text{ use Parseval's identity to find } \int_0^\infty \left( \frac{\sin t}{t} \right)^4 dt.\)
\(\text{If } f(x) = e^{-a|x|} \text{ and } F(s) = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{a}{s^2+a^2}, \text{ use Parseval's identity to find } \int_{-\infty}^\infty \frac{dx}{(x^2+a^2)^2}.\)

\(\text{Using Parseval's identity and the Fourier transform of the rectangular pulse } f(x) = \begin{cases} 1, & |x| \leq a \\ 0, & |x| > a \end{cases}, \text{ prove that } \int_0^\infty \left( \frac{\sin t}{t} \right)^2 dt = \frac{\pi}{2}. \text{ What is the value of } \int_0^\infty \left( \frac{\sin(at)}{t} \right)^2 dt?\)
\(\text{Parseval's identity for Fourier transforms states that:}\)

sq.q: \(\text{State and prove Parseval's identity for Fourier transforms.}\)
answer: \(\text{Proof: Start from convolution theorem with } g(x) = \overline{f(-x)}\)

Step Marks Let \(f(x) = e^{-|x|}\), then \(F(s) = \mathcal{F}\{e^{-|x|\}\} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \cdot \frac{1}{1+s^2}\) (3) Parseval's identity: \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} |f(x)|^2 dx = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} |F(s)|^2 ds\) (2) LHS: \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-2|x|} dx = 2\int_{0}^{\infty} e^{-2x} dx = 2 \cdot \frac{1}{2} = 1\) (3) RHS: \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \left( \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \cdot \frac{1}{1+s^2} \right)^2 ds = \frac{2}{\pi} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{ds}{(1+s^2)^2}\) (3) Thus \(1 = \frac{2}{\pi} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{ds}{(1+s^2)^2}\) (2) Therefore \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{ds}{(1+s^2)^2} = \frac{\pi}{2}\) (2)
